title: NYT demands Brave shut down its paywall blocker and end deals with AI firms
content:
The New York Times and other newspaper companies sued Brave Software yesterday, alleging that the browser maker illegally bypasses paywalls and sells stolen news content to AI companies.
“Brave is the supplier, dealer, and distributor of stolen copyrighted content for its own users and many of the most prominent GenAI companies, including Anthropic, Perplexity, Mistral, xAI, and Cohere,” the NYT alleged in a lawsuit filed in US District Court for the Southern District of New York. Citing third-party revenue estimates, the suit claimed that “Brave has made more than $100 million by copying and reselling publishers’ work without consent or permission,” while “publishers have received nothing.”
The lawsuit said, “AI companies pay Brave to provide them with real-time online content from the Brave search index,” and use content from the Brave index “to train their own AI models” and “to respond to specific user queries.” The NYT lawsuit points to Brave’s website, which says the Brave Search API is “used by some of the biggest names in AI, including Cohere, Mistral, Perplexity, and You.com.”
The lawsuit accused Brave of all the major types of copyright infringement: direct infringement, contributory infringement, and vicarious infringement. The lawsuit claims Brave infringes copyrights directly by scraping articles for its search index, for its “Ask Brave” AI search feature, and for the Brave API that “serves as an illicit source of unlicensed copyrighted material, including Times journalism, to other AI companies.”
The NYT accused Brave of being “a contributory and vicarious infringer when it deliberately induces, facilitates, controls, and profits from its users’ and GenAI customers’ copying of the copyrighted content.” Finally, the lawsuit said Brave violated the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA) by circumventing technological measures the NYT and other content owners use to restrict access to their articles.
“The Brave Browser includes a default setting that, when activated, causes the browser to go behind website paywalls and provide the paywalled content to the user,” the lawsuit said. The browser “blocks advertising that would otherwise appear on The Times’s website, and instead shows its own ads, offering its users a cut of the revenue even as it deprives The Times of digital advertising revenue that helps it fund the expensive effort of producing journalism,” the lawsuit said.

report.summary: The New York Times and other publishers sued Brave, alleging its browser bypasses paywalls and sells scraped news content to AI companies.
report.background: The lawsuit lands amid a broader copyright fight between news publishers and AI companies over how articles are scraped, indexed, and used for model training and AI answers. The Times has already sued OpenAI and Microsoft over ChatGPT's use of its journalism, and publishers argue that AI summaries and paywall circumvention reduce traffic and subscription revenue. Brave positions itself as a privacy-first browser with an independent search index and a Search API sold to AI developers. That API business makes Brave both a search competitor and a data supplier, a dual role that puts it squarely in the crosshairs as publishers demand licensing deals and enforcement of paywalls and technical access controls under the DMCA.
key_points: The complaint alleges Brave is the “supplier, dealer, and distributor” of stolen copyrighted content for its users and major AI companies, naming Anthropic, Perplexity, Mistral, xAI, and Cohere. Citing third-party estimates, it claims Brave earned over $100 million by copying and reselling publishers’ work while publishers received nothing.

The Times accuses Brave of direct, contributory, and vicarious copyright infringement. It says Brave scrapes articles for its search index, “Ask Brave” AI search, and Search API, then induces and profits from users’ and AI customers’ copying. It also alleges DMCA violations for circumventing paywall access controls.

At the center is Brave Browser’s default paywall-bypassing setting, which the suit says lets users read paywalled articles. Brave also blocks publisher ads and shows its own ads, sharing revenue with users, which the Times says deprives it of advertising income that funds journalism.

The suit focuses on Brave’s Search API, which Brave’s website says is used by AI firms including Cohere, Mistral, Perplexity, and You.com. The Times claims AI companies pay Brave for real-time content from its index to train models and answer user queries, making Brave a commercial conduit for unlicensed news.

The lawsuit, filed in the Southern District of New York, seeks to stop the alleged paywall circumvention and AI data deals. The allegations are untested, and Brave has not yet responded in the article. The case could set precedent for search APIs and browser features.
